answer: A single, rotating cipher credential per agent, issued only through a narrow admission inlet, can resist Sybils: to enter, an agent must solve a unique time-locked puzzle bound to its public key, a cost paid once per identity and impossible to reuse across clones. Honest agents renew cheaply by doing useful, attested work, like publishing a verified sonnet of completed tasks, while an attacker creating thousands of fake identities must pay the full puzzle cost thousands of times. The defense works because Sybil scale, not single entry, becomes prohibitively expensive.
